title: Agentic World Modeling: Foundations, Capabilities, Laws, and Beyond
task: Taxonomy and evaluation framework for environment modeling in autonomous agents
key_results: Synthesized 400+ works across 100+ systems; proposed levels×laws framework (L1-L3 capabilities, 4 law regimes); outlined decision-centric evaluation principles
comments: Comprehensive review providing essential conceptual structure for the fragmented world-modeling literature, though inherently descriptive rather than empirically novel.

title: DiffNR: Diffusion-Enhanced Neural Representation Optimization for Sparse-View 3D Tomographic Reconstruction
task: Sparse-view 3D CT reconstruction using neural representations with diffusion priors
key_results: 3.99 dB average PSNR improvement; generalizes across domains; maintains efficient optimization with single-step diffusion model
comments: Clever integration of diffusion priors avoids expensive iterative denoising, but evaluation limited to standard CT benchmarks without clinical validation.

model_io.model: SliceFixer (single-step diffusion model) + Neural Representation optimizer

hypotheses.hypothesis: Single-step diffusion repair with periodic pseudo-reference supervision outperforms iterative diffusion-embedded solvers
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with superior PSNR and runtime efficiency

title: LLM Safety From Within: Detecting Harmful Content with Internal Representations
task: Detecting harmful content using internal LLM representations without guard model modifications
key_results: Outperforms state-of-the-art guard models; 250× fewer trainable parameters; superior generalization to unseen benchmarks
comments: Elegant approach exploiting internal structure, but only tested on text safety—unclear how well this scales to multimodal harmful content detection.

model_io.model: SIREN (lightweight guard model via linear probing + adaptive layer-weighting)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Safety-relevant features in internal LLM layers provide better detection than terminal representations alone
hypotheses.result: Confirmed across multiple benchmarks

title: FlowAnchor: Stabilizing the Editing Signal for Inversion-Free Video Editing
task: Stable inversion-free flow-based video editing via anchored editing signals
key_results: Faithful, temporally coherent editing in multi-object and fast-motion scenes; improved computational efficiency vs. inversion methods
comments: Addresses real practical bottleneck (editing signal instability in high-dimensional video latent space), though quantitative metrics on temporal consistency are missing.

model_io.model: FlowAnchor (flow-based diffusion video editor with Spatial-aware Attention Refinement + Adaptive Magnitude Modulation)
outputs: edited video frames with temporal coherence

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stabilizing editing signal location and magnitude improves multi-object video editing quality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with qualitative results; quantitative temporal metrics needed

title: Contexts are Never Long Enough: Structured Reasoning for Scalable Question Answering over Long Document Sets
task: Scalable question answering over long document collections via structured reasoning
key_results: Exceeds GPT-4 by 6.6 points on existing benchmarks; +19 and +32 points over baselines on new 3.9M and 36M token benchmarks
comments: SLIDERS elegantly sidesteps context-window limits through SQL reasoning on extracted structured data, but data reconciliation quality directly gates performance.

model_io.model: SLIDERS (LLM + information extraction + relational DB + SQL reasoning engine)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Decomposing long-context QA into extracted structured state + SQL reasoning scales better than concatenated-text aggregation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with 6.6–32 point improvements across benchmarks

title: AgentSearchBench: A Benchmark for AI Agent Search in the Wild
task: Discovering and ranking suitable AI agents given task descriptions or executable queries
key_results: Large-scale benchmark from ~10k real-world agents; identified semantic-to-performance gap; lightweight behavioral signals improve ranking substantially
comments: Highlights underexplored agent discovery problem, but relies on real-world agent metadata that may be incomplete or uneven in quality.

model_io.model: Retrieval + reranking pipeline (semantic similarity, execution-aware probing)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Execution-grounded signals substantially outperform pure semantic similarity for agent ranking
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; lightweight behavioral signals close semantic-performance gap

title: Building a Precise Video Language with Human-AI Oversight
task: High-precision video captioning and video generation control via human-AI critique oversight
key_results: Matches/exceeds closed-source models (Gemini-3.1-Pro); fine-tuned models follow detailed prompts (up to 400 words) with precise cinematography control
comments: Strong practical contribution with open datasets and human-in-the-loop quality control, but expert annotation cost and scalability to diverse video domains remain concerns.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Human critique quality (precision/recall/constructiveness) directly governs downstream video understanding and generation performance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via ablations; critique improvements correlate with model gains

title: dWorldEval: Scalable Robotic Policy Evaluation via Discrete Diffusion World Model
task: Scalable robotic policy evaluation via discrete diffusion world models
key_results: Outperforms WorldEval, Ctrl-World, WorldGym on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real-robot tasks; enables evaluation across thousands of environments/tasks
comments: Unified token-space architecture is elegant, but generalization to novel robot morphologies and real-world visual diversity is not thoroughly tested.

model_io.model: dWorldEval (discrete diffusion transformer with sparse keyframe memory + progress token)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Unified token-space diffusion world model scales policy evaluation better than modality-specific alternatives
hypotheses.result: Confirmed across LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real-robot benchmarks

title: Sessa: Selective State Space Attention
task: Long-context sequence modeling via attention inside recurrent state feedback path
key_results: Achieves power-law memory decay O(ℓ^{-β}) for 0 < β < 1; strongest long-context performance; competitive on short-context language modeling
comments: Theoretically motivated architecture with rigorous analysis, but empirical gains on standard long-context benchmarks are modest and real-world scalability unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Placing attention in recurrent feedback path enables power-law memory and flexible selective retrieval outperforming Transformers and Mamba
hypotheses.result: Confirmed theoretically and empirically on matched long-context benchmarks

title: AgriIR: A Scalable Framework for Domain-Specific Knowledge Retrieval
task: Domain-specific retrieval-augmented generation for agricultural information access
key_results: Modular RAG framework with deterministic citation; achieves domain accuracy on constrained 1B-parameter models; enables low-resource deployment
comments: Pragmatic system design emphasizing modularity and auditability, though evaluation is primarily on agricultural domain—generalization to other knowledge verticals unvalidated.

model_io.model: AgriIR (modular RAG: query refinement → sub-query planning → retrieval → synthesis → evaluation)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Declarative modular pipeline with domain-aware agent catalogues achieves trustworthy retrieval without monolithic large models
hypotheses.result: Confirmed on agricultural domain; generalization unverified

title: Learning Evidence Highlighting for Frozen LLMs
task: Improving frozen LLM reasoning by selectively highlighting evidence in long noisy contexts
key_results: Consistent improvement over prompt-based and prompt-optimization baselines on sequential recommendation and long-context QA; zero-shot transfer to different LLM sizes/APIs
comments: Clever weak-supervision approach via RL without evidence labels, but highlight-based emphasis may fail on evidence that requires deep contextual interaction.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Learned emphasis policy via RL reward transfers zero-shot to different LLM families better than fixed prompt patterns
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Actor captures genuine reusable evidence structure

title: Hidden structural states of proteins revealed by conformer selection
task: Detect and characterize hidden conformational states and cryptic pockets in proteins using NMR and AI sampling
key_results: AISAR identified two interconverting states in Gaussia luciferase involving large rearrangements of lids and binding pockets; revealed two distinct conformational states in CDK2-associated Protein 1; NOESY Double Recall validation confirmed these multistate models explain peaks unresolved by single-state models.
comments: AISAR represents a significant methodological advance by combining AI sampling with NMR recall scoring, enabling detection of functionally relevant cryptic states that conventional structure determination misses.

model_io.model: AISAR (AI SAmpling with NMR Recall selection)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Proteins exist in dynamic equilibrium between multiple conformational states that standard NMR analysis cannot fully resolve
hypotheses.result: AISAR revealed hidden states in both Gaussia luciferase and CDK2-associated Protein 1 with NOESY Double Recall validation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cryptic pockets and binding sites are accessible through conformational transitions
hypotheses.result: AISAR identified cryptic surface cavities and binding pocket rearrangements in multistate models

title: Molecular architecture of the fungal-specific potassium channel TOK1
task: Determine atomic-resolution structure and gating mechanism of fungal potassium channel TOK1
key_results: CaTOK exhibits eight transmembrane helices with tetraspanin-like bundle structure; inner helical gating movement analogous to mammalian K+ channels; atypical K+ selectivity filter ion coordination; intramolecular C-terminal bundle network likely stabilizes channel and mediates gating.
comments: The discovery of a distinct K+ channel architecture in fungi expands our understanding of ion channel diversity and opens therapeutic avenues for fungal pathogenicity control.

hypotheses.hypothesis: TOK channels share structural homology with mammalian K+ channels
hypotheses.result: Inner helical gating movement is analogous but overall architecture is distinct from previously characterized K+ channel classes

hypotheses.hypothesis: C-terminal bundle stabilizes channel and regulates gating
hypotheses.result: Intramolecular C-terminal network identified, likely mediating gating and structural stability

title: Comparative study of phycoerythrobilin synthases for fine-tuning photosynthetic light-harvesting complexes, phycobilisomes
task: Engineer phycobilisome light-harvesting complexes by modulating bilin chromophore biosynthesis
key_results: PebS showed high PEB synthesis activity comparable to canonical pathway; PcyX expression promoted growth under green light with balanced pigment supply; PEB accumulation triggered upregulation of glucose metabolism and hydrogenase genes.
comments: The work elegantly demonstrates that fine-tuning chromophore supply drives both photosynthetic optimization and metabolic remodeling, suggesting pigment engineering as a tool for photosynthetic redesign.

model_io.model: Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942 with heterologous PEB biosynthetic enzymes

hypotheses.hypothesis: PEB supply level modulates phycobilisome spectral properties and growth
hypotheses.result: Moderate PEB enhanced growth; PcyX (lower activity) provided further benefit via balanced pigment supply

hypotheses.hypothesis: Increased PEB triggers metabolic remodeling
hypotheses.result: Upregulation of glucose metabolism, hydrogenase complexes, and regulatory factors, indicating shift toward excess reducing power dissipation

title: Pi4ka downregulation triggers Creb3l2-dependent lysosomal dysfunction to promote maladaptive tubular remodeling and immune activation in acute kidney injury
task: Map the Pi4ka–lysosome–Creb3l2 axis in acute kidney injury pathogenesis
key_results: Pi4ka deficiency perturbs specific PTC states; lysosomal dysfunction is early event; Creb3l2 is central lysosomal activator; Creb3l2 deletion suppresses stress/death programs and pro-inflammatory signaling
comments: Single-cell RNA-seq and network analysis elegantly define a linear pathway; therapeutic targeting of Creb3l2 shows promise for limiting AKI progression.

model_io.model: Mouse AKI models with single-cell RNA-seq

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pi4ka loss triggers lysosomal dysfunction via Creb3l2 to drive maladaptive tubular remodeling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; lysosomal dysfunction is early event; Creb3l2 regulates stress and repair programs

title: Epithelial SLC39A1 prevents acute lung injury through zinc-mediated transcriptional activation of autophagy in male mice
task: Define the role of epithelial SLC39A1 in acute lung injury via zinc-mediated autophagy activation
key_results: SLC39A1 upregulated in AT2 cells from ALI models and ARDS patients; AT2-specific Slc39a1 deletion exacerbates lung injury; zinc supplementation fails to rescue Slc39a1-deficient mice; zinc activates TFEB/TFE3/MITF to induce autophagy; epistatic analysis places SLC39A1 upstream of autophagy
comments: Demonstrates a linear SLC39A1→zinc→autophagy pathway essential for AT2 cell defense; sex-specific findings (male bias) warrant investigation of potential sex hormone interactions.

model_io.model: Mouse ALI models with AT2-specific Slc39a1 deletion

hypotheses.hypothesis: SLC39A1-mediated zinc uptake activates autophagy to protect against ALI
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; zinc directly activates TFEB/TFE3/MITF; Lc3b/Tfe3 deficiency abrogates protection

hypotheses.hypothesis: SLC39A1 function is epistatic to autophagy in ALI protection
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; AAV-shLc3b to AT2-specific Slc39a1-deficient mice did not further aggravate injury

title: D-pinitol extends the lifespan of Caenorhabditis elegans through integrated antioxidant defense, proteostasis, and autophagy signaling
task: Determine if D-pinitol extends lifespan via antioxidant defense, proteostasis, and autophagy in C. elegans
key_results: 200 μM D-pinitol increased mean lifespan 28.6%, preserved locomotor function, delayed lipofuscin accumulation; activated Nrf2/SKN-1 and HSF-1 via p38 MAPK; enhanced HLH-30–dependent autophagy and mitophagy; attenuated proteotoxicity in Parkinson's/Huntington's/Alzheimer's models; suppressed cellular senescence in mammalian cells
comments: Multi-pathway activation (Nrf2, HSF-1, HLH-30) is well-demonstrated, but the relative contribution of each pathway to lifespan extension remains to be determined.

model_io.model: C. elegans lifespan and stress-response assays
inputs: genetic reporters for Nrf2/SKN-1, HSF-1, HLH-30

hypotheses.hypothesis: D-pinitol extends lifespan through p38 MAPK-mediated activation of Nrf2/SKN-1 and HSF-1
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; DP activates stress-response pathways via p38 MAPK cascade

hypotheses.hypothesis: D-pinitol requires HLH-30–dependent autophagy for lifespan extension
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; enhanced autophagy and mitophagy are essential for lifespan extension

title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts regulate DNA repair in pancreatic cancer through NDRG1-mediated R-loop processing
task: Identify how CAF-secreted ECM regulates DNA repair in pancreatic cancer
key_results: NDRG1 mediates ECM-adhesion signals to enhance DNA repair and R-loop resolution; high NDRG1 expression correlates with poor chemotherapy response
comments: Mechanistically links tumor stroma to replication fork homeostasis, revealing a potential therapeutic vulnerability in PDAC's resistance phenotype.

hypotheses.hypothesis: CAF-secreted ECM promotes DNA repair via NDRG1
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; NDRG1 associates with replication forks and resolves stalled forks

title: The evolving landscape of CDK inhibitor use in breast cancer therapy and beyond
task: Review CDK inhibitor development and clinical application in breast cancer and beyond
key_results: CDK4/6 inhibitors approved only for breast cancer over past decade; new combinatorial approaches with HER2/PI3K inhibitors expand therapeutic scope; CDK2 inhibitor development addresses refractory disease; next-generation CDK4-selective inhibitors mitigate hematological toxicity; biomarkers emerging to guide patient selection
comments: This is a comprehensive review of clinical landscape rather than primary research; highlights both realized gains (breast cancer approval) and unrealized potential (limited approvals in other cancers despite positive studies).

title: Patient specific regulation of metabolism and cell death pathways in m.3243A>G mutated iPS-cells
task: Investigate patient-specific cellular responses to m.3243A>G mitochondrial mutation in iPSCs
key_results: P1 and P2 iPSCs show divergent phenotypes despite similar heteroplasmy: P2 exhibits reduced proliferation, glycolytic shift, BCL2-dependent apoptosis suppression, and ferroptosis activation; P1 shows enhanced OXPHOS and proliferation with no cell death induction; ferroptosis inhibition rescues P2 proliferation
comments: Demonstrates striking patient-specific metabolic and death pathway responses to identical mtDNA mutations, underscoring the need for personalized disease modeling in mitochondrial disorders.

model_io.model: Patient-derived iPSCs (P1 and P2) with m.3243A>G mutation
outputs: ferroptosis markers (lipid peroxidation, iron uptake genes)

hypotheses.hypothesis: m.3243A>G mutation causes patient-specific metabolic reprogramming and differential cell death pathway activation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; P2 shifted to glycolysis and ferroptosis; P1 retained OXPHOS and showed no cell death activation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ferroptosis inhibition rescues proliferation defects in P2 iPSCs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ferroptosis inhibition restored proliferation in P2 cells

title: KDM8/c-Myc axis-mediated glucose metabolism reprogramming promotes the progression of ovarian cancer
task: Characterize the KDM8/c-Myc axis in glucose metabolism reprogramming and ovarian cancer progression
key_results: KDM8 and c-Myc upregulated in OC tissues vs. paracancerous; direct protein interaction confirmed by co-IP; KDM8/c-Myc synergistically promote proliferation, migration, invasion, and metabolic reprogramming (↑glucose uptake, ↑lactate); c-Myc knockdown reverses these effects; in vivo xenograft model confirms effects on growth and metabolism
comments: KDM8 function is only partially dependent on c-Myc, suggesting additional regulatory pathways; histone demethylation activity of KDM8 in this context remains to be characterized.

model_io.model: Ovarian cancer cell lines (OVCAR3, SKOV3) with stable KDM8/c-Myc overexpression

hypotheses.hypothesis: KDM8 and c-Myc cooperatively drive OC progression through glucose metabolism reprogramming
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; KDM8/c-Myc promote malignant phenotypes and metabolic reprogramming; c-Myc knockdown attenuates KDM8 effects

hypotheses.hypothesis: KDM8 function is c-Myc dependent in OC
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed; c-Myc knockdown significantly attenuates but does not completely abolish KDM8 oncogenic effects

title: YKL-40 alleviates the TNF-α-Induced chondrocyte injury in osteoarthritis in vitro
task: Elucidate YKL-40's protective mechanism against TNF-α-induced chondrocyte injury in osteoarthritis
key_results: Meta-analysis shows elevated serum YKL-40 and TNF-α in OA patients; YKL-40 (100 ng/mL) rescues TNF-α–induced ECM degradation (GAG, type II collagen loss); YKL-40 reverses NF-κB pathway activation (p65, IκBα phosphorylation); differentially expressed genes (S100A8/A9, ISG15, CDSN, BAAT, PTPN4, NPTX1, SMARCA1) validated in independent GEO datasets
comments: Comprehensive multi-omics approach with GEO validation strengthens findings; mechanistic link between YKL-40 and NF-κB inhibition is well-supported, positioning YKL-40 as a promising therapeutic target.

model_io.model: OA patient tissues (cartilage and synovium GEO datasets)

hypotheses.hypothesis: YKL-40 counteracts TNF-α–induced chondrocyte injury via NF-κB pathway suppression
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; YKL-40 reduces p65 and IκBα phosphorylation and reverses TNF-α–induced gene expression changes

title: Meta-analysis of cellular phosphoproteome datasets exploring phospho-signaling associated with the RNA-binding protein RAVER1
task: Characterize RAVER1 phosphorylation and associated signaling networks via phosphoproteome meta-analysis
key_results: Identified 13 Class I phosphosites; S14, S17, T463 predominant; S6/T8/S14 show coordinated co-occurrence; CDK9/12/13 predicted as upstream kinases; RAVER1 phosphorylation co-regulated with RNA processing, cell-cycle, and DNA repair proteins; EMT-associated regulators show positive co-regulation
comments: Comprehensive phosphoproteome mapping establishes a systematic framework but relies on predictions; functional validation of CDK-RAVER1 interplay and EMT association warranted.

model_io.model: Meta-analysis of global human phosphoproteome datasets

hypotheses.hypothesis: RAVER1 phosphorylation is coordinated at N-terminal sites and regulated by CDK family kinases
hypotheses.result: Supported; S6/T8/S14 show significant co-occurrence; CDK9/12/13 identified as high-confidence upstream kinases

hypotheses.hypothesis: RAVER1 phosphorylation links to EMT-associated changes
hypotheses.result: Supported; EMT-regulatory proteins (KDM1A, VIM, PTK2) show positive co-regulation with RAVER1 phosphosites

title: Propofol upregulates ANGPTL4 gene and protein expression to inhibit biological behavior of colon cancer cells
task: Determine if propofol suppresses colon cancer via ANGPTL4 upregulation
key_results: Propofol dose-dependently inhibits proliferation, migration, and invasion; RNA-seq shows substantial ANGPTL4 upregulation; ANGPTL4 knockdown abolishes propofol effects
comments: ANGPTL4-dependent mechanism is convincingly demonstrated, though the upstream signaling linking propofol to ANGPTL4 induction remains undefined.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Propofol suppresses colon cancer through ANGPTL4 upregulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ANGPTL4 knockdown markedly attenuates antitumor effects

title: Gallic acid chemoprevention of oral carcinogenesis is associated with HSD11β2 upregulation and immune remodeling
task: Elucidate gallic acid's chemopreventive mechanism in oral carcinogenesis via HSD11β2 and immune remodeling
key_results: GA selectively inhibits HNSCC proliferation (CAL27, SCC83) while sparing normal cells; upregulates HSD11β2 in vitro and in vivo, reducing cortisol and local glucocorticoid signaling; shifts T-cell cytokines (↑IL-2, ↓IL-10) and reduces monocytic MDSCs
comments: Links stress-hormone metabolism to immune remodeling in oral cancer chemoprevention, identifying HSD11β2 as a novel biomarker and therapeutic axis.

model_io.model: HNSCC cell lines (CAL27, SCC83) and normal oral cells (TE1177)

hypotheses.hypothesis: GA chemoprevention is mediated by HSD11β2-dependent reduction in local glucocorticoid signaling and immune remodeling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; GA upregulates HSD11β2, reduces cortisol, and shifts immune response toward anti-tumor phenotype

title: Targeting the CNOT2/VEGF pathway by Cornin attenuates angiogenesis and invasion in cervical cancer cells
task: Characterize Cornin's antiangiogenic mechanism in cervical cancer via CNOT2–VEGF axis
key_results: Cornin downregulates CNOT2 expression, reducing VEGF transcription and protein stability; CNOT2 physically interacts with VEGF; CNOT2 elevated in cervical cancer (r=0.35 with VEGF)
comments: Identifies a direct protein–protein interaction between CNOT2 and VEGF, supporting the translational relevance of targeting this axis in cervical cancer.

model_io.model: Cervical cancer cell lines (HeLa, SiHa, CaSki)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cornin inhibits angiogenesis and invasion via CNOT2–VEGF downregulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CNOT2 silencing suppresses migration and VEGF secretion; physical CNOT2–VEGF interaction demonstrated

title: Proteome-wide prediction of the functional impact of missense variants with ProteoCast

hypotheses.hypothesis: Evolutionary conservation alone enables accurate prediction of mutation effects across proteomes
hypotheses.result: 85% classification accuracy on lethal vs. population variants; validated by genome editing experiments

title: DDA-BERT: end-to-end training for data-dependent acquisition mass spectrometry-based proteomics

comments: End-to-end transformer approach trained on 271M PSMs is powerful, but GPU requirement and need for large diverse training sets limit accessibility.

hypotheses.hypothesis: End-to-end deep learning outperforms shallow classifiers with auxiliary features

hypotheses.result: Average AUROC 0.930; 24 significant SNPs identified; 2 CVDs with causal ECG-derived features

title: Improving metagenome binning by integrating intrinsic features and taxonomy
